A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NeuronLens research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated content.

before.justification: v2 reports original activation-distribution measurements, concept-erasure experiments, and intervention, hyperparameter, and layer ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds linguistic-concept, steering, and SAE experiments, particularly in Appendices K, M, and N.

M1.justification: The mean-plus/minus-tau-times-standard-deviation gate and adaptive dampening remain unchanged. v3 adds range-gated steering and an SAE-feature adaptation with activation-frequency filtering (Appendices M.2 and N), providing limited procedural extensions to the existing framework.

E1.justification: Appendix K adds token-completion evaluations involving pronouns, punctuation, delimiters, and subject–verb agreement. This substantially extends coverage beyond v2's dataset-class concepts and general-capability measurements. All five original classification datasets remain.

E2.justification: v3 adds evaluated activation-steering and directional-ablation comparators in Tables 28–30, substantially broadening the intervention comparisons. The original Max, Probe, Probeless, dampening, and mean-replacement comparisons remain represented.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce 500 samples per linguistic concept with a 400/100 split, probeless ranking, layer-14 steering with a=-2, and range masking with tau=1. Appendix N introduces Gemma-2-2B with 16k/65k SAE configurations and feature-selection controls. These are additional experimental designs; the main classification protocol is retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds Llama activation-distribution analysis, pairwise-overlap measurements, and LLM-assisted text case studies comparing activation-range centers and boundaries. Mean-replacement analysis also expands to AG-News and Emotions. Existing layer, tau, and adaptive-dampening analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or intervention significance tests. Existing trimmed-mean and practical-normality reporting practices remain; predictive confidence and activation standard deviations are not newly introduced uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: The five classwise classification tables retain their values, but v3 adds substantial linguistic, steering, SAE, and distributional results. New Table 32 reports 16k-SAE perplexity increases of 9.510 for feature masking and 0.958 for range masking. v2's IMDB/SST2 perplexity–MMLU rows and classwise saliency-comparison scores are omitted.

T1.justification: The activation-range mathematics, ideal erasure condition, and adaptive-dampening formula are retained. Renaming CR to AR, adding pseudocode, and stating standard steering/projection formulas do not introduce substantive theoretical reasoning, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: v3 removes the explicit first-comprehensive-study priority claim and the introductory 'up to 7x' interference-reduction claim. Its abstract specifies neuron-level masking as the comparator. The central Gaussian-range attribution and reduced-collateral-interference contributions remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations of semantic transitions across activation ranges, residual polysemanticity in SAE features, and steering failure cases. It qualifies stability under full masking as smooth degradation. The fixed-tau limitation stated in v2 Appendix B is removed from v3 Appendix A.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code repository link, end-to-end pseudocode, Gemini Pro case-study procedures, linguistic-data curation and splits, steering parameters, and SAE configuration and feature-selection details. Existing training and hardware disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: Beyond v2's brief SAE future-work remark, v3 develops substantial positioning relative to dictionary learning, SAEs, clustered neuron explanations, and steering. Section 6 adds discussions of La Rosa, Kopf, and several SAE/control works, explicitly positioning NeuronLens as complementary to learned sparse representations.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Datasets and models move earlier, Section 5 separates range attribution from causal validation, and the existing appendices undergo substantial reordering and consolidation.

P2.justification: The TMLR format substantially changes typography and figure placement. v3 adds Llama plots, colored text-example tables, pseudocode, and numerous experimental tables; it restructures the main results display and relocates existing GPT-2 material. The DBPedia box plot is redrawn, although its caption retains inconsistent neuron/class counts.

improvement.justification: The linguistic-completion and SAE studies substantially strengthen evidence that range selectivity extends beyond v2's dataset-class labels and raw neurons. Steering comparisons, explicit pseudocode, and code-access information improve evaluation and reproducibility. These gains outweigh lost result detail and reporting inconsistencies, including Appendix K versus Table 22's verb choices and Figure 7's outdated caption; those issues still limit confidence in parts of the added material.
